title: Arsenal’s Jurrien Timber has ‘chance’ to play again this season – Mikel Arteta
content:
Mikel Arteta says there is a “chance” that Jurrien Timber plays again for Arsenal this season, but that he does not know how big that chance is.

The 24-year-old right-back was forced off with a groin injury in the first half of Arsenal’s 2-0 win over Everton in March, and is yet to make a return.

Arsenal manager Arteta has previously stated the issue was more complicated than first expected, but with Ben White out for the season with a medial ligament injury, the need for options at right-back increases.

Asked whether there is a chance Timber can play again this season, Arteta said: “There is a chance, but being completely honest, I cannot tell you how big that chance is. He’s going to try to do everything he can to try to convert that chance in the shortest possible period.”

The Netherlands international was pictured with the team in club gear during their trip to West Ham last weekend, despite not being available.

On how the injury is evolving now, Arteta added: “It’s progressed a little bit in the last few days. He’s feeling better. We’re going to try to get him fit and available as quickly as possible but let’s see. He’s been out for a while.

“He’s such an important player for us. We all know that and he’s doing everything he can to help the team in any capacity. We know (about) his leadership, his quality, and how much the team needs him. He’s trying everything that he can.”

White’s knee injury will keep him out for the rest of Arsenal’s season, but on whether it will rule him out of the World Cup for England, Arteta said: “We have to wait and see. It looks like a long-term injury.

“At the moment, the focus is when we can have him back to be available for Arsenal and that’s not going to happen in many, many weeks.”

Left-back Riccardo Calafiori was also replaced due to injury away to West Ham, and on his fitness, Arteta said: “We don’t know whether he is going to be available or not. We still have (four) days ahead. Hopefully it’s nothing serious but we will have to wait and see how he reacts.”

Arteta’s initial response to White’s injury against West Ham was to move Declan Rice to right-back, before introducing Cristhian Mosquera for the second half.

Rice previously impressed in the role against Brighton & Hove Albion in December, particularly with what he brought to Arsenal in attack. However, at the London Stadium, the movement of him from midfield left Arsenal exposed and allowed West Ham to gain momentum.

Rice’s return to midfield and Mosquera coming on as the more natural deputy at right-back rectified this, but even so, Arteta is keeping his options open for how he will replace White in the coming weeks.

Mosquera has filled in at right-back throughout the season, but asked whether that is now the 21-year-old’s position, Arteta said: “There are different options in relation to the opponent and what we want to do with certain players.

“We need to be open to that. Not only to one, but to two or three options because games can vary and players can pick up injuries. We need to be flexible and think about other options.”

Aside from Rice’s cameos at right-back, Calafiori played a half in that position in a 2-0 win over Paris Saint-Germain in October 2024.

On whether his skillset is transferable to both flanks, Arteta said: “The sample is so tiny, so it’s very difficult to judge a player when they’re had such low minutes (in a position).

“It’s the same when we played Thomas Partey there. We had some really good moments, so others when you don’t win and (the judgement) is it’s because Thomas played as a full-back. Declan Rice was exceptional against Brighton, but the other night was something else.

“The sample is so little and it will remain that way from here until the end of the season to judge whether a player is good enough or can perform in the position. And what is the cost of moving a player from one position to another? That is the balance we need to find.”

William Saliba also made a handful of appearances at right-back while at Saint-Etienne and Marseille, but has not been used there under Arteta. Any movement of him would break the chemistry between himself and Gabriel at the heart of Arsenal’s defence and require considerations over opportunity cost.

Comparisons may be drawn between moving Myles Lewis-Skelly from left-back to midfield this month, but Arteta said: “With Myles it was a bit different. It was a choice because of what we saw and what we believed he could do and what the team was needing.”

Based on the consistency Arsenal found before White’s injury against West Ham, keeping as many players in the same position as possible seems as though it would be the most logical decision.

While others may provide more attacking threat than Mosquera, the young defender has been reliable in the main. Allowing him to stay in the role will also keep some of the balance that Arsenal have found when progressing the ball through other areas of the pitch.

Arsenal’s next game being on Monday, May 18, will not only help Arteta from a player availability perspective but also to figure out his best approach. But as the last couple of weeks have shown, sometimes acting on a feeling rather than thoughts works out best.
